subject: bmc-mtcollins1 host side (Ampere Mt. Collins, Foxconn build)
observed_from: UEFI Interactive Shell v2.2 / EDK II / UEFI v2.70 (American Megatrends, 0x0005000F), reached over IPMI SOL after the host fell through its boot options
why_taken_here: the kernel configuration for a stateless host image depends on the actual NIC driver, and PXE reporting Arch:00011 establishes firmware network support rather than which Linux driver binds the adapter. Taken from firmware rather than a running Linux because no shell was reachable in the installer that was booted at the time.

ethernet.identification: Intel I350 Gigabit Ethernet, dual port
ethernet.note: the two functions correspond to the two ports; the host NIC that attempted PXE reported MAC 28-C1-3C-8A-D6-4A on serial

graphics.note: the host image uses the serial console; no DRM/framebuffer driver is required

usb.note: this is the path the BMC virtual media arrives on; firmware consumes it during boot, so a kernel driver is needed only if the running host must read the medium after boot

pci.mass_storage_note: no mass-storage controller appears in the enumeration, which is the hardware-level confirmation that this unit is diskless rather than merely unpartitioned

secure_boot.consequence: an EFI image presented to this unit needs no signature and no key enrollment; a signing policy is not a prerequisite for the host image, though enabling Secure Boot later would make one

pxe.observed_line: Start PXE over IPv6 on MAC: 28-C1-3C-8A-D6-4A / PXE-E16: No valid offer received
pxe.consequence: PXE is present in firmware and unusable today because nothing on this LAN answers it. A network boot route therefore requires standing up DHCP/TFTP or HTTP service before it can be a transport, which is why virtual media remains the proven route.
pxe.http_boot_status: NOT ESTABLISHED. Firmware offers 'Press <F12> to PXE Boot' and no HTTP Boot device was observed. Whether this firmware carries the UEFI HTTP Boot driver is a separate measurement, taken in Setup or from the boot-device list, and is not implied by PXE support.

alpine_iso_negative.evidence: the UEFI shell mapping table lists BLK0 at PcieRoot(0x60000)/Pci(0x3,0x0)/Pci(0x0,0x0)/USB(0x5,0x0)/USB(0x0,0x0) with NO FS alias, so firmware saw the medium as a block device and found no filesystem it could mount. Boot option loading failed and the firmware fell through to the shell.
alpine_iso_negative.what_it_does_not_establish: that the ISO is malformed. It establishes that THIS firmware, over ITS virtual-USB-CD presentation, did not map an EFI system partition from it. Ubuntu's arm64 live-server ISO boots by the same route on the same unit, so the difference is in how the two images lay out their EFI boot path, not in the transport.
alpine_iso_negative.consequence_for_the_host_image: a derived virtual-media envelope must be verified to present an ESP this firmware maps -- an EFI/BOOT/BOOTAA64.EFI on a FAT filesystem the firmware recognises -- rather than assumed to work because it is an ISO
